trials.name: TANGO
trials.population: Mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer's disease or mild Alzheimer's disease
trials.primary_endpoint: Percentage of Participants With Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
trials.results_summary: The trial was terminated for futility after BIIB092 failed to show clinical benefit on the primary efficacy measure (CDR-SB) compared to placebo at Week 78. The safety profile was comparable to placebo.

trials.name: PASSPORT
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in Progressive Supranuclear Palsy Rating Scale (PSPRS) at Week 52
trials.results_summary: Failed to meet primary efficacy endpoint on the PSPRS at Week 52, leading to the discontinuation of the PSP development program for gosuranemab.

trials.name: CN002-003
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety and Tolerability as Measured by Percentage of Participants with Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
trials.results_summary: Safety and tolerability were established across multiple ascending intravenous doses, supporting advancement to Phase 2 trials.

trials.name: CN002-001
trials.primary_endpoint: Safety and tolerability, as measured by incidence of AEs, serious AEs, AEs leading to discontinuation, and death
trials.results_summary: Single ascending doses were found to be safe and well-tolerated in healthy volunteers.

related_evidence.description: TANGO: a placebo-controlled randomized phase 2 study of efficacy and safety of the anti-tau monoclonal antibody gosuranemab in early Alzheimer's disease.
Safety and efficacy of anti-tau monoclonal antibody gosuranemab in progressive supranuclear palsy: a phase 2, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (PASSPORT).
Safety of the tau-directed monoclonal antibody BIIB092 in progressive supranuclear palsy: a randomised, placebo-controlled, multiple ascending dose phase 1b trial.

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence strongly supports the document's conclusion that BIIB092 (gosuranemab) lacks efficacy in slowing cognitive and functional impairment in early Alzheimer's disease. The Phase 2 TANGO trial (NCT03352557) was robustly designed (quadruple-blind, placebo-controlled) but was terminated for futility when the treatment failed to show clinical benefit on the CDR-SB compared to placebo. This failure mirrors the drug's earlier clinical trajectory in another tauopathy; the Phase 2 PASSPORT trial (NCT03068468) for progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) was similarly halted due to a lack of efficacy. Peer-reviewed publications for both the TANGO and PASSPORT studies confirm that while the antibody was generally well-tolerated and lowered N-terminal tau in cerebrospinal fluid, it did not translate to cognitive or functional benefits, resulting in the discontinuation of gosuranemab's development.
